title: Set up your first business
summary: Understand the steps from owner account to workspace.

sections.title: Follow the setup sequence
paragraphs: Start with the owner account, then enter your business name, type and location. The owner and business are separate: one user may manage multiple businesses.
Choose your goals, optionally add a public profile, then select a plan. Wallet, loyalty and staff setup come after payment or trial activation.

sections.title: Know when setup is complete
paragraphs: Only a confirmed payment or trial can unlock the ready step and workspace. Selecting a price is not a subscription activation.
In the development preview, account and plan steps are illustrative. Do not use it as proof that a business account or subscription exists.

title: Keep your business details clear
summary: Find the right place for business and public presentation settings.

sections.title: Review your business profile
paragraphs: Open Settings in the workspace to review the business details. Keep the name and location recognisable to customers.
The business profile and the owner account describe different things. Update each in its own section.

sections.title: Prepare the public presentation
paragraphs: Open Customer Page to edit the public description, branding and contact links. Use the preview to check how a customer will see them.
Production saving, media uploads and public slug availability need the backend. A local preview is not a published page.

title: Prepare your Customer Page and business QR
summary: Use one public entry point for the customer experience.

sections.title: Configure the page
paragraphs: Open Customer Page in the dashboard. Review your description, contact information, social links and visual branding.
The page presents the business and available programmes or offers. Configure those in their own workspace sections; do not duplicate them in the description.

sections.title: Share the right entry point
paragraphs: The public page uses /b/{business slug}. Its business QR opens this same experience. QR and poster presentation come from the Customer Page configuration.
A public business page and a private customer profile are different. The backend handles customer identification, account linkage and activation. Preview changes are not evidence of publication.

title: Prepare a loyalty programme
summary: Understand configuration, rewards and customer progress.

sections.title: Choose the programme structure
paragraphs: Open Loyalty to review a stamp or points programme and its reward. Keep the explanation and eligibility clear to the customer.
Use local drafts to review the configuration. A draft does not award points or stamps to anyone.

sections.title: Read customer progress correctly
paragraphs: Customer progress comes from confirmed business records. The frontend does not calculate earned loyalty or turn a visit into a sale.
Reward eligibility and redemption require backend validation. Do not treat illustrative previews as live balances.

title: Understand digital cards
summary: Learn how saving a card differs from receiving notifications.

sections.title: Follow the customer path
paragraphs: Customers enter through the business QR or link and open the Customer Page. After joining an available programme, they can use a supported Wallet save action.
Apple Wallet and Google Wallet need a valid card or provider URL issued for the customer. If no action is available, a preview cannot issue a real pass.

sections.title: Understand updates
paragraphs: A pass update can change displayed programme information. It is separate from a notification being delivered.
Notifications depend on provider support, the device and customer settings. Delivery on every device is not guaranteed.

title: Read customer records and activity
summary: Use the customer list, profiles and analytics without guessing results.

sections.title: Find the customer
paragraphs: Open Customers to review the business-scoped list. Select a customer to see their profile, available contact information and recorded activity.
Contact edits in development are tab-local drafts. They do not create visits, sales or customer history.

sections.title: Interpret the records
paragraphs: Visits, inactivity, loyalty, memberships and spending come from the business backend. A recorded visit is not automatically a sale.
An empty list means no customer data is available for this business. Example records, where shown, are illustrative.

title: Prepare staff access and scanning
summary: Distinguish the business entry QR from a customer identification QR.

sections.title: Choose the correct QR
paragraphs: The business QR opens the public Customer Page. The customer QR identifies the customer during a staff workflow.
Use the Staff section to review the scanning interface. In production, access and allowed actions depend on confirmed staff permissions.

sections.title: Confirm the result
paragraphs: A scan alone is not proof that a visit was recorded. The backend must validate the customer, business and permitted action.
Development previews do not accrue loyalty or create visit history. Staff roles and permissions are enforced by the backend.

title: Prepare an offer without publishing it
summary: Review content and distribution before a live campaign exists.

sections.title: Prepare the draft
paragraphs: Open Offers to review the customer-facing offer, then Campaigns to prepare campaign content and intended channels.
Keep the title, description and customer entry link consistent. Social distribution depends on supported platform authorisation.

sections.title: Separate preview from publication
paragraphs: Development campaign drafts stay in the current tab. Previewing or saving a draft does not publish to social networks or send Wallet updates.
A live campaign needs backend publishing, platform permissions and a confirmed result. The integrations screen must receive a valid authorisation action before an account can be connected.

title: Compare plans and understand activation
summary: Know what displayed prices and limits mean.

sections.title: Compare the catalog
paragraphs: Open Pricing to compare monthly and annual display prices, active-customer limits, locations and explicitly listed features.
Not specified is not the same as unavailable or unlimited. The current catalog does not define every entitlement.

sections.title: Confirm before activation
paragraphs: Choosing a plan does not charge a card or activate a subscription. Payment or trial activation needs confirmation from the backend.
Final pricing, availability and access come from the production plan catalog. Do not treat a development plan selection as a billing record.
